newsitem.title: LEBANON: Hizbollah condemns Arafat for "false accusations".
newsitem.headline: Hizbollah condemns Arafat for "false accusations".

text.p: Lebanon's Hizbollah on Sunday denounced Palestinian President Yasser Arafat for "spreading lies" suggesting that the group may be linked to a twin suicide attack in Jerusalem last month.
A Hizbollah official in turn accused Arafat's supporters of firing Katyusha rockets into northern Israel on Friday, a day before Israeli planes attacked a Hizbollah camp in Lebanon.

"Arafat has unleashed a series of false accusations and lies targeting Hizbollah and naming it in the course of a campaign coordinated with the Zionist entity (Israel)," the pro-Iranian group said in a statement.

Arafat told CNN and Abu Dhabi television that a claim of responsibility issued in the name of Hamas after the July 30 bombing in Jerusalem had contained a call for the release by Israel of kidnapped Hizbollah cleric Sheikh Abdel Karim Obeid.
"What is the relation of Hizbollah with this terrorist activity unless they were behind it or they knew it or they facilitated....it?" Arafat asked.
He said senior Israeli officers had told him that they believed the suicide bombers, whose identity has not been established, came from abroad.

The Hizbollah statement, faxed to an international news agency in Beirut, noted that the timing of Arafat's accusations "met the daily reccurrent Zionist aggressions against our people in different Lebanese areas".

Violence has escalated last week along the Israel-Lebanon border. Fourteen people, seven of them Lebanese civilians, have been killed in Israeli air raids, artillery shelling or bombs planted by unknown assailants since Monday.

"This is a clear indication that Arafat is justifying these Zionist crimes committed against our people and that he and his authority have become a tool in the service of Zionist terrorism," Hizbollah's statement added.

In the eastern Lebanese town of Baalbek, a senior Hizbollah official attending the funeral of a guerrilla killed in one of the Israeli air raids, accused Arafat's supporters of firing Katyusha rockets into Israel on Friday.

"Arafat and his supporters are behind the Katyusha firing into northern Palestine. They did it to give them (Israeli forces) a justification to hit us," said Sheikh Mohamad Yazbek, Hizbollah's top leader in the Baalbek area.

Israeli planes rocketed a Hizbollah camp south of Baalbek on Saturday killing a guerrilla and wounding four a day after hitting a Palestinian base south of Beirut following a Katyusha attack on northern Israel in which a woman was wounded.
Hizbollah said it did not fire the rockets.
Lebanese Foreign Minister Faris Bouez also accused Arafat on Saturday of assisting Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu in inflaming the situation in south Lebanon.
Some 360,000 Palestinian refugees live in 12 camps across Lebanon, many belonging to anti-Arafat factions opposed to the current peace accords with Israel.
